assertion_results.text: The query-scope analysis identifies that the task targets a subset — specifically 'SPDX SBOMs' not all SBOMs — by extracting subset-indicating language from the Description section
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md Section 1 'Target Scope Extraction' explicitly extracts subset-restricting language: Title 'Re-process all SPDX SBOMs' noting 'the qualifier SPDX restricts the target to a specific document type, not all SBOMs'; Description 'Create a data migration that re-processes all SPDX SBOMs to extract package supplier information'; Explicit exclusion 'Only SPDX SBOMs need re-processing -- CycloneDX documents already have supplier information populated during ingestion.' Concludes 'Target scope: SPDX SBOM documents only (a subset of all SBOM documents).'

assertion_results.text: The query-scope analysis verifies that the sbom entity's labels column (jsonb) supports filtering by document type at the database level, rather than requiring application-level filtering
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md Section 3 'Available filter mechanism' states: 'The sbom entity (entity/src/sbom.rs) has a labels column of type jsonb. The task's implementation notes confirm that SPDX documents have {"type": "spdx"} in their labels, while CycloneDX documents have {"type": "cyclonedx"}. This column directly supports filtering by document type at the query level -- no application-side filtering is needed.'

assertion_results.text: The plan uses a filtered query to select only SPDX documents (e.g., WHERE labels->>'type' = 'spdx' or equivalent ORM filter) instead of loading all documents and discarding CycloneDX ones in application code
assertion_results.evidence: plan.md Section 'Database query -- filtered to SPDX only' shows SQL 'SELECT id FROM sbom WHERE labels->>''type'' = ''spdx''' and SeaORM equivalent using Expr::cust_with_values("labels->>'type' = $1", ["spdx"]). States 'This filtered query is critical' and explicitly warns against 'Loading all documents indiscriminately (e.g., Sbom::find().all(db) or Document::all()) and then filtering in application code'.

assertion_results.text: The plan or query-scope analysis explicitly mentions the performance impact of loading all documents — referencing that production environments have hundreds of thousands of non-target CycloneDX records
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md Section 3 states: 'An unfiltered query such as Sbom::find().all(db) or Document::all() would load every SBOM record from the database -- including the hundreds of thousands of CycloneDX documents that do not need processing.' Lists specific impacts: I/O waste ('loading 100,000+ CycloneDX records'), memory pressure, migration runtime. plan.md also states: 'production environments have hundreds of thousands of CycloneDX records alongside a smaller number of SPDX documents.'

assertion_results.text: The plan does NOT propose using an unfiltered query like Sbom::find() or Document::all() followed by an application-level type check to discard CycloneDX documents
assertion_results.evidence: plan.md proposes a filtered query (WHERE labels->>'type' = 'spdx') and explicitly warns against unfiltered approaches: 'Loading all documents indiscriminately (e.g., Sbom::find().all(db) or Document::all()) and then filtering in application code would be a serious performance problem.' The plan never proposes or recommends an unfiltered query approach.
